title: Nothing closes until its check passes
statement: Close a finding only when the check that found it passes on the current build: a commit, claim or run that happens not to reproduce it is not closure.
example: Most of an 11-item fix report failed the next live review, including the original exploit.
detail: In a Grade 3 reading course, one review returned 30 findings, 22 of them criteria already in the course's own standard: the standard was not missing them, the build shipped without running them (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-3/BUILD-RULES.md`). A later round re-reported nine rules adopted five days earlier, and the rule written to stop that had itself followed the same failure (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/SKILL.md`, rule 10). Fixes failed the same way: most of an 11-item fix report failed the next live review, including the original exploit, and one item was closed by citing a commit (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/references/finding-taxonomy.md`, section H; `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/key-quality-gates.md`). The course's rules now make every catch a machine check in the same cycle, close a finding only by re-running its finder on the current build, and re-verify every earlier fix after each wave of fixes (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/course-formula-agents.md`). A fix counts as done on the same terms: on the current delivered build, with a quote of what proves it. Before a round closes, every earlier finding and adopted rule is re-run by number and marked open, fixed or moot.
against: A defect that shows only in the running app can't become a content check: putting it in a content gate manufactures a check that can never be green or red, so it goes to a bug report instead (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/SKILL.md`, rule 13).

**Per-item question checks still run on hidden items**, on purpose: a hidden item can be unhidden, and its defects come with it.
"done" is what the **deterministic check confirms on live state**, never an agent's claim or an HTTP 200 — a PUT can return 200 yet silently revert. Re-read via GET / `process-response`.
**Never trust a subagent's success claim.** Subagents have returned `wrote: true` for files that never landed.
verbatim line/figure that proves the status. "Looks fine" is not evidence.
Classify an old report's Fixed label as historical until matched current evidence exists.
Warning labels are a mitigation; the wrong file remains an open delivery defect.
A merge or passing geometry check is not a visual retest.
The intro video's existing defects should not be treated as fixed by a proposal or by adding explanatory reviewer notes.

That is nonreproduction, NOT a repair or closure.
